afterFields.description: Soft delete and purge protection are separate safeguards. Soft delete is enabled by default for new vaults and cannot be disabled after enablement; purge protection must be enabled explicitly. Select the 7-90 day retention period at creation because it cannot subsequently be changed. Recovering a vault does not restore deleted role assignments or Event Grid subscriptions.

Another reason is that if the IP addresses in the AKS subnet are a scarce resource, consuming its IP addresses for services will reduce the maximum scalability of the cluster .

after.name: wafsg-ApplicationGatewayCapacityChangesApplicationGatewayCapacityRequirements
after.title: Be aware of Application Gateway capacity changes when enabling WAF
after.description: When WAF is enabled, every request must be buffered by the Application Gateway until it fully arrives, checks if the request matches with any rule violation in its core rule set, and then forwards the packet to the backend instances. When there are large file uploads (30MB+ in size), it can result in a significant latency. Because Application Gateway capacity requirements are different with WAF, we do not recommend enabling WAF on Application Gateway without proper testing and validation.

beforeFields.title: Create segmentation through isolation boundaries to contain breach: Apply identity segmentation. For example, implement role-based access control (RBAC) to assign specific permissions based on roles. Follow the principle of least privilege to limit access rights to only what's necessary. afterFields.description: Assign least-privilege identities and choose isolation boundaries for apps and plans according to the data and trust boundaries. Use private endpoints or other supported inbound restrictions, configure the outbound routing explicitly, and verify allowed flows. Consider App Service Environment when dedicated compute and network isolation are required.

beforeFields.description: Secrets are kept separate from your app's configuration. App settings are encrypted at rest. App Service also manages secret rotations.
beforeFields.title: (App Service) Always use Key Vault references as app settings.

afterFields.description: Prefer managed identities to avoid secrets where possible. For remaining secret-valued app settings, authorize the app's identity to read the required vault secrets and ensure network reachability. Versionless references pick up newer secret versions within 24 hours because App Service caches values; version-pinned references do not automatically follow the latest version. Do not store ordinary nonsecret configuration in Key Vault, and isolate environment-specific references with appropriate slot settings.

beforeFields.description: Custom domains enable secure communication through HTTPS using Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol, which ensures the protection of sensitive data and builds user trust.
beforeFields.title: (App Service) Configure custom domains for applications.  Disable HTTP and only accept HTTPS requests.

afterFields.description: Configure certificate bindings for the intended hostnames and enable HTTPS Only to redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS. Test trust, hostname matching, expiration and renewal; the portal's Secured label alone does not verify these properties. HTTPS Only is a redirect control, not evidence that the shared HTTP port is closed. Validate minimum TLS requirements and any proxy-to-origin encryption separately.

beforeFields.description: Get the security benefits of using an Azure virtual network. For example, the application can securely access resources within the network.   Add a private endpoint to help protect your application. Private endpoints limit direct exposure to the public network and allow controlled access through the reverse proxy.
beforeFields.title: (App Service) Configure the application for virtual network integration.  Use private endpoints for App Service apps. Block all public traffic.  Route the container image pull through the virtual network integration. All outgoing traffic from the application passes through the virtual network.

afterFields.description: Use private endpoints and restrict public access when the application should be reached only through approved private paths or a reverse proxy. Configure virtual network integration for outbound connectivity, and explicitly route application traffic and container-image pulls through the intended network. Verify DNS, identity permissions, firewall rules and required platform dependencies. Enabling virtual network integration alone is not proof that every outbound or inbound path is private.
